grid.title: Gold nanoparticles: {size} by UV-visible spectrophotometry
grid.unknown: the plasmon peak and the particle size of {size}

size.label: a 10 nm colloid
size.note: A 10 nm colloid is a clear ruby red and its plasmon band sits near 517 nm, close to the small-particle limit where the peak hardly moves with size at all.

source.title: Haiss, Thanh, Aveyard and Fernig, Anal. Chem. 79 (2007) 4215: lambda_spr = 512 + 6.53 exp(0.0216 d) and d = exp(3.00 A_spr/A450 - 2.20), fitted for spherical citrate-capped gold from about 5 to 100 nm

size.label: a 30 nm colloid
size.note: At 30 nm the band has moved only a few nanometres to the red, but it has grown noticeably taller against the 450 nm absorbance - which is why the ratio, not the peak position, is the better size measure for small particles.

source.title: Haiss, Thanh, Aveyard and Fernig, Anal. Chem. 79 (2007) 4215: lambda_spr = 512 + 6.53 exp(0.0216 d) and d = exp(3.00 A_spr/A450 - 2.20), fitted for spherical citrate-capped gold from about 5 to 100 nm

size.label: a 60 nm colloid
size.note: A 60 nm colloid looks distinctly less red and more purple, and its band has moved well past 530 nm: here the peak position itself becomes a useful size measure.

source.title: Haiss, Thanh, Aveyard and Fernig, Anal. Chem. 79 (2007) 4215: lambda_spr = 512 + 6.53 exp(0.0216 d) and d = exp(3.00 A_spr/A450 - 2.20), fitted for spherical citrate-capped gold from about 5 to 100 nm

size.label: a 90 nm colloid
size.note: By 90 nm the colloid is purple and the band is broad and far to the red. This is the top of the range the relations were fitted over; beyond it, and for any particle that is not a sphere, they must not be used at all.

source.title: Haiss, Thanh, Aveyard and Fernig, Anal. Chem. 79 (2007) 4215: lambda_spr = 512 + 6.53 exp(0.0216 d) and d = exp(3.00 A_spr/A450 - 2.20), fitted for spherical citrate-capped gold from about 5 to 100 nm
